Baryogenesis

Words: 34
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
Baryogenesis is the dynamical production of the cosmic excess of baryons over antibaryons. It requires baryon-number violation, C and CP violation, and departure from thermal equilibrium, or an appropriate generalization of these Sakharov conditions.

ρ˙​+3aa˙​(ρ+P)=0.
(1)

Barotropic equation of state

Words: 166 Articles: 5
Cosmological perfect-fluid continuity equation OurBigBook.com
A constant barotropic equation of state has P=wρ. The cases w=0 and w=1/3 describe pressureless matter and radiation respectively.

a(t)=[1+23​(1+w)H0​(t−t0​)]2/[3(1+w)].

Pressureless matter

Barotropic equation of state OurBigBook.com
Pressureless matter has equation-of-state parameter w=0, energy density ρ∝a−3 and negligible stress compared with its rest-mass density.

Cosmological density parameter (Ω)

Critical density OurBigBook.com
The density parameter is Ω=ρ/ρcrit​. In a Friedmann universe, its departure from one measures the spatial-curvature term relative to the density or expansion term.

Flatness problem

Words: 47 Articles: 1
Cosmological density parameter OurBigBook.com
In a decelerating expanding universe, ∣Ω−1∣ grows, so its small present value requires extremely fine-tuned early initial data unless an earlier mechanism drives Ω toward one.
Inflationary solution of the flatness problem
Words: 21
Flatness problem OurBigBook.com
The continuity equation gives
dtd​(ρa2)=−Ha2(ρ+3P).
(8)
During expansion with ρ+3P<0, the product ρa2 grows and ∣Ω−1−1∣∝(ρa2)−1 decreases.

Horizon problem

Words: 47
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
In a decelerating hot Big Bang model, widely separated regions of the observable universe have nearly equal conditions despite having no shared past light cone. Inflation supplies an earlier era with a shrinking comoving Hubble radius, allowing a formerly causal patch to grow beyond the later horizon.

Particle horizon

Words: 45
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
The particle horizon at cosmic time t is the greatest comoving distance from which a light signal could have reached an observer since the initial time:
χph​(t)=∫tinitial​t​a(t′)cdt′​.
(9)
Regions separated by more than twice this distance cannot have exchanged signals by time t.

Dark energy

Cosmology OurBigBook.com
Dark energy is a smooth component with sufficiently negative pressure to drive accelerated cosmic expansion.

Cosmological constant (Λ)

Words: 31
Dark energy OurBigBook.com
The cosmological constant Λ is the constant term proportional to the metric in the Einstein field equations. Interpreted as vacuum energy, it has PΛ​=−ρΛ​, so its energy density is constant during expansion.

Matter density (ρm​)

Words: 27
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
The matter density ρm​ is the energy density in nonrelativistic matter. In a homogeneous expanding universe, conservation of particle number and dilution of physical volume give ρm​∝a−3.

Big Crunch

Words: 17
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
A Big Crunch is a future finite-time singularity in which a recollapsing universe reaches vanishing scale factor.

Cosmic inflation

Words: 1k Articles: 50
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
Cosmic inflation is an early period of accelerated expansion, often modeled by a scalar field whose potential energy dominates its kinetic energy.

Number of e-folds (N=log(a/ai​))

Cosmic inflation OurBigBook.com

N=logai​af​​=∫ti​tf​​Hdt.

Primordial perturbation

Words: 28
Cosmic inflation OurBigBook.com
A primordial perturbation is an early-universe fluctuation that seeds later cosmic microwave background anisotropy and large-scale structure. Inflation generates scalar curvature perturbations and tensor perturbations from quantum fluctuations.

The matter power spectrum contains low-amplitude oscillatory features because baryons preserve their pre-recombination acoustic phase and later transfer part of it gravitationally to the combined matter distribution.

The Alcock-Paczyński test compares radial and transverse distance conversion using a feature that is statistically isotropic in comoving space.

Alcock-Paczyński test OurBigBook.com
The Alcock-Paczyński parameter compares radial and transverse distance conversion at one redshift. An intrinsically isotropic comoving feature obeys
ΔθΔz​=H(z)χ(z),
(158)
so its unknown absolute size cancels.

Lambda-CDM model (ΛCDM model)

Words: 17
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
The Lambda-CDM model combines a cosmological constant with cold dark matter and the standard baryonic and radiation components in an expanding Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker metric.

Dark matter

Words: 77 Articles: 2
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
Dark matter is matter inferred from its gravitational effects that does not emit, absorb, or scatter enough electromagnetic radiation to account for those effects as ordinary baryonic matter.

Cold dark matter (CDM)

Words: 21
Dark matter OurBigBook.com
Cold dark matter is nonrelativistic early enough that its primordial free-streaming length is small compared with the cosmological structures of interest.

Warm dark matter (WDM)

Words: 28
Dark matter OurBigBook.com
Warm dark matter has a primordial collisionless free streaming length large enough to suppress the formation of low-mass haloes, while remaining nonrelativistic early enough to cluster on galactic and larger scales.

Matter-radiation equality

Words: 54 Articles: 1
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
Matter-radiation equality is the epoch at which the background matter and radiation densities are equal. Its horizon wavenumber keq​ sets the turnover scale of the cold-dark-matter transfer function.

Matter-radiation equality scale (keq​)

Words: 25
Matter-radiation equality OurBigBook.com
The matter-radiation equality scale is the comoving horizon wavenumber at equality. Modes at larger wavenumber entered during radiation domination and had their matter growth suppressed.
